slides.headline:
Seoul wants to stay
open all night.
slides.subline: One neighborhood closes to sightseeing at 5 p.m., and has fined people for it since March 2025

slides.label: The only hours tourists may enter the Red Zone around Bukchon-ro 11-gil. Outside 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., sightseeing there carries a 100,000 won fine

slides.title:
A city opening up,
a street shutting down.
slides.body:
In August 2026 Seoul announced a plan to run as a 24-hour destination: a nighttime economy from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m., a target of 30 million foreign visitors and five trillion won more in annual night spending within five years, 269 sports facilities open to midnight, and a late-night 'Firefly Bus' linking Hongdae, Gwanghwamun, DDP, Myeong-dong and Gangnam from October.

Bukchon is the exception, and it is a legal one. Jongno-gu designated it a Special Management Area on 1 July 2024 under the Tourism Promotion Act — the tool a Korean district uses when a residential area is being worn down by its own popularity.

items.t: Red Zone — visits only 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
items.d: A 34,000 sq m residential hanok block around Bukchon-ro 11-gil. Entering for tourism outside those hours is a 100,000 won fine

items.t: Orange and Yellow Zones — no time limit
items.d: The rest of the area. Orange gets active on-street guidance, Yellow gets monitoring. No fine attaches to the hours there
Vehicles over 16 seats are barred from a 2.3 km stretch of Bukchon-ro, Bukchon-ro 5-gil and Changdeokgung 1-gil. Fines began 1 January 2026
Patrol staff the district calls 'Bukchon sheriffs' explain the rule on the spot. The penalty follows only if you stay on after the warning

slides.title:
What this means
if you're visiting

items.d: The golden hour on Bukchon-ro 11-gil is the hour you may not be there for. Arrive after 10 a.m., leave by 5 p.m.

items.t: Being there is not the offense — sightseeing is
items.d: Residents and their families, shop customers, hanok-stay guests and people simply passing through are all exempt. Photographing and wandering are what the rule targets

items.t: Only one lane is a Red Zone
items.d: Most of Bukchon has no hour limit at all. The restriction is narrow, not a village-wide curfew, whatever a blog headline says

items.t: Arrive on foot or by subway
items.d: Anguk Station on Line 3 is a few minutes away. A chartered coach cannot legally drop you on the main lanes

slides.text:
A neighborhood is not
an attraction that closes.
It is where people live.
slides.by: That is the premise of the designation, and the early signs are that it has not emptied the place out. Jongno-gu reports noise, congestion and complaints down since the restrictions began, and Korea Real Estate Board figures put vacancy among medium and large shops in Bukchon at 1.9% in Q3 2025, against 6.2% a year earlier. The chartered-bus pilot was made permanent in February 2026. This post is research, not a personal visit — every figure comes from a published source, checked on 17 October 2026.

caption:
Seoul spent August announcing that it wants to be a 24-hour city — a nighttime economy running 6 p.m. to 6 a.m., 30 million foreign visitors and five trillion won more in night spending inside five years, 269 sports facilities open until midnight, and a late-night Firefly Bus linking Hongdae, Gwanghwamun, DDP, Myeong-dong and Gangnam from this month.

One neighborhood is going the other way, and it has the law behind it. Jongno-gu designated Bukchon a Special Management Area on 1 July 2024 under the Tourism Promotion Act. Inside the Red Zone — a 34,000 sq m residential hanok block around Bukchon-ro 11-gil — tourists may visit only between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. Come outside those hours to sightsee and the fine is 100,000 won. That has been enforced since 1 March 2025, after a four-month guidance period. Buses over 16 seats are barred from a 2.3 km stretch of Bukchon-ro, Bukchon-ro 5-gil and Changdeokgung 1-gil, with 300,000 won fines from 1 January 2026; the pilot was made permanent in February 2026.

Three things the headlines tend to flatten. The restriction covers one lane, not the village — the Orange and Yellow zones have no hour limit. Being present is not the offense: residents and their families, shop customers, hanok-stay guests and people walking through are exempt, and the rule targets sightseeing and photographing. And you get a warning first — district patrol staff explain the rule on the spot, and the penalty follows only if you stay.

The practical version is simple. The golden hour you wanted on that lane is the hour the rule exists to protect, so go mid-morning instead, and come on foot or by subway from Anguk Station. Early signs say the trade worked: Jongno-gu reports noise and complaints down, and shop vacancy in Bukchon fell to 1.9% in Q3 2025 from 6.2% a year earlier. Sources in the last slide.
